hanna.title: The Off-Duty Ledger
hanna.text:
Hanna traps you at a corner table in the bakery with two mugs of cider and a thick sheaf of guild forms. She's annotated them in bright blue ink.

"Business meeting," she says. "Very serious. Sit."

Half the pages are real. They're bounty tallies, with her corrections. The other half are something else. There's a hand-drawn seating chart of the guild hall. It shows which adventurers tip best, which merchants blush when you compliment them, and who has been seen leaving whose room.

In one margin there's a small doodle of a hooded figure. It's labeled "Terrible disguise. 10/10 charm."

You're reading it upside down. She catches you and slaps the paper flat. The freckles across her nose have gone bright pink.

"Trade secrets! Eyes on your pastry, Sam!" She pulls the whole stack toward her side of the table. "That one's old, anyway. It's from before I knew you. I've got much better material now."
ngpp: Right next to the hoodie doodle she pauses with a sudden squint, muttering that she could've sworn she drew a little lantern beside it before.
"Okay, creepy question," she mutters over her cider, squinting at her own ink. "Did I already tell you that hoodie disguise joke? Why'd my hand write 'still 10/10' under it?"
"Don't laugh," she says softly, sliding the blue-ink ledger halfway toward you. "Every page in this stack feels like notes from a life we already lived, Sam. Tell me I'm not losing it."

choices.label: Demand to see the rest of your margin notes
choices.res: She tries to swat your hands away, fails, and ends up laughing into her cider while giving you a wildly exaggerated dramatic reading of every rumor she ever heard about you.

choices.label: Ask why she really left the Guild desk
choices.res: Her grin softens into something real. "Because standing behind a counter hearing everyone else's stories gets old, Sam. I wanted to actually live in one for a change."

image.comp: leaning over a bakery table shielding a stack of annotated parchment sheets, freckled cheeks flushed, laughing brightly
image.setting: warm corner bakery table by a sunlit window, mugs of cider

hanna.title: Filing Error
hanna.text:
You open the washroom door on the assumption that nobody is in there.

Hanna is perched on the rim of the tub in a thin towel. One damp blonde curl is plastered across her eyebrow. She has a stack of soaked index cards, and she's drying them one at a time over a candle stub.

She yelps. The cards very nearly go back into the water.

Then she recovers, and narrows her eyes at you. It's pure theater.

"Knock much?! I could have been doing anything in here!" She's holding a card over the flame by one corner. It's starting to smoke. "And before you ask, no, these aren't about you."

She looks at the card in her hand.

"Mostly."

She turns it face down on her knee. You saw the first word on it before she did, and it was your name.

1.text:
You push open the washroom door. Hanna is sitting sideways on the rim of the bath in a short towel, with wet curls sticking to her freckles. She puts her stack of cards down, dry side up.

She doesn't yelp. She gives you a sly, breathless grin, and hooks one finger into the pocket of your hoodie.

"Terrible timing, Sam." She tugs you a step closer. "Unless you've finally come to give me that interview. I've got a lot of questions, and I'd rather not ask them with my clothes on. I do my best work face to face."

choices.label: Step into the steam and claim her live interview at the tub rim
choices.res: "Best filing error all week," she breathes as your mouth finds hers through the steam.

choices.label: Leave her to dry her cards with a promise for later
choices.res: "I'm holding you to that after hours," she calls brightly behind the latch.

3.text:
You open the washroom door. Hanna is up to her chest in hot bubbles, with her wet gold hair piled up and one curl hanging over her grin.

She sees you. She lifts one bare foot out of the water, sets it against the door, and kicks the latch shut herself. Then she stands up in the tub. Foam slides down off her tits and her stomach, and she lets you watch it go.

"Knock? Please. You know the bath schedule by heart." She crooks a finger. "Get your shirt off and get in here, Sam. I've been thinking about your cock all afternoon, and the water won't stay hot forever."

choices.label: Climb straight into the steaming bath under her
choices.res: She laughs softly against your lips as her slick thighs settle astride your hips in the bubbles.

choices.label: Wash the soap across her shoulders and tease her about gossip
choices.res: She melts back against your chest with a happy groan. "Okay, better than any ledger."

choices.label: Apologize and shut the door fast
choices.res: "Smooth exit!" she calls through the wood. Five minutes later she slides a single dry index card under your door reading: IOUs: 1 proper knock (collectable tonight).

choices.label: Ask which card has your name on it
choices.res: Hanna smirks, deliberately letting the towel dip an inch at her collarbone as she holds a card between two fingers. "Depends—are you offering a live interview?"

else.res: "Classified!" she announces, tossing a wet sponge straight at your chest before slamming the latch shut with a bright laugh.

choices.label: Offer to hold the candle so she doesn't burn the cards
choices.res: "Now that's executive support," she grins, tugging the towel tight around her thighs while you lean politely against the doorframe.

image.comp: perched on the rim of a wooden bath wrapped in a towel, holding damp index cards near a candle, startled playful grin

hanna.title: After Last Call
hanna.text:
The common room is dark except for one low lantern behind the counter. Hanna is sitting on a tall stool with her shoes off, swinging her legs and counting the night's tips into neat brass stacks.

She's been talking since you came down. It's about the cook's feud with the fishmonger, and a knight who has been in three times this week and won't say why.

You lean on the bar beside her. The talking slows down, and then it stops.

She reaches out and straightens your collar with light, warm fingers. She doesn't take her hand away afterward.

"Funny thing," she says quietly. She's looking at your shirt button and not at your eyes. "I spent five years at that desk writing down everybody else's secrets. I knew the whole town's business. Nobody knew a thing about me. I made sure of it." Her thumb moves on your collar. "I never realized how nice it'd be when somebody already knew mine."

choices.label: Cover her hand with yours on your collar
choices.res: Her fingers curl into your shirt at once, freckles glowing in the amber light. "Yeah," she whispers, leaning forward until her forehead rests against your chin. "Like that."

choices.label: Lock the front bolt and lift her onto the empty bar
choices.res: Brass coins clatter across the counter as she hooks her ankles straight behind your waist.

choices.label: Pour two nightcaps and stay by the counter
choices.res: She hops down to sit on the counter right beside you, bumping her knee against yours while the quiet house settles around you both.

image.comp: sitting on a dark wooden bar counter barefoot by a single lantern, adjusting his collar with a quiet tender smile
image.setting: quiet pleasure-house bar after closing, single amber lantern

hanna.title: Head Clerkship
hanna.text:
A messenger from the Adventurers' Guild comes by before noon with a letter stamped in red wax.

The head clerk has retired. The Guildmaster wants Hanna back. He's offering double her old pay, a corner office of her own, and a seat on the trade council.

She reads it twice on the front steps. She's twirling her pencil between her knuckles as she goes, faster and faster, and on the second read-through it snaps in half.

She looks up at you. For once there's no teasing in her face.

"It's everything I thought I wanted, two years ago," she says softly. "I used to lie awake planning what I'd do with that office. I had the curtains picked out."

She turns the two halves of the pencil over in her palm.

"I walked out because I was sick of knowing everybody's story and not having one. I've got one now. Say the word, Sam. What do you think I should do?"
ngpp: Staring at the red wax seal, she snaps her pencil right on beat—then blinks down at the wood as though remembering the exact crack.
"Weirdest déjà vu," she mutters softly over the offer letter. "Why does double pay already sound like bad news compared to staying on your porch?"
"Look at me holding a fancy corner-office scroll and already tearing the corner," she says quietly, freckles warm. "I already chose you over that marble desk once, Sam. Didn't even have to think."

choices.label: "I'd hate to lose you, yet I won't hold you back."
choices.res: Hanna exhales slowly, then laughs—a little wetly—and crumples the red-wax offer into her pocket. "Good answer, Sam. Mostly because I'd already decided not to go."

choices.label: "Stay here with me. This place isn't half as bright without you."
choices.res: Her face lights up bright enough to outshine the porch lantern. She grabs the messenger's ink pen, scribbles "Position already filled—by me, somewhere better" across the bottom, and hands it back.

choices.label: "Double pay is hard to argue with."
choices.res: Her smile goes flat in half a second. "Right. Good business sense." She walks inside without waiting for you—though when morning comes, she is still behind your desk, quiet and unusually distant.

image.comp: standing on porch steps holding an official red-wax guild letter and a snapped pencil, serious hopeful expression
image.setting: lantern-lit wooden front steps in daylight

hanna.title: Off the Market
hanna.text:
Hanna drags you up the bell tower above the market street just before sunset. She's got a bag of warm honey almonds, and she sits down at the overlook with it between her knees.

The evening lamps are coming on all across Hollowmere. Down below, the guild hall doors open, and the adventurers spill out toward tavern row in twos and threes.

She used to know every one of them. She could have told you their tabs and who they were sweet on. From up here she could still point out who's avoiding whom.

She leans her head on your shoulder and sighs.

"Look at them all," she says lazily. "Sixteen parties. I can count about forty rumors from here. See those two by the fountain? Something's definitely going on there." She eats an almond. "And for once I don't care. I've spent my whole life watching other people's stories from behind a counter. The best one in town is sitting right next to me, and I'm in it."

choices.label: Kiss her temple and pull her closer
choices.res: She turns her face up before you can pull away, catching your mouth in a warm, sweet kiss that tastes like honey and dusk.

choices.label: Tell her you're glad she walked out on the Guild
choices.res: "Best impulse decision I ever made," she says happily, lacing her fingers tight through yours until the stars come out.

image.comp: sitting on a stone tower ledge at sunset leaning her head on his shoulder, overlooking a lantern-lit fantasy town
image.setting: stone clocktower overlook at sunset above glowing city rooftops

hanna.title: Front Page
hanna.text:
Hanna shuts your bedroom door with her heel and leans back against it.

She's wearing your spare shirt and nothing else. It comes halfway down her thighs. She's grinning, bright-eyed and out of breath, and the sight of her goes through you like heat.

She crosses the rug in four steps and climbs into your lap on the edge of the bed. Her hands come up to frame your face.

"I've been writing this down all week," she whispers. "I couldn't get it right, so I'm just going to say it."

She presses her forehead to yours. Her hips settle against you.

"No more margin notes. No more rumors. I'm done standing behind somebody else's counter and writing about what other people get." Her breath is warm on your mouth. "I want the whole thing, Sam. Every week, every cycle, and nothing kept back. I know everybody's secret in this town. Mine is that I'm in love with you. Tell me I'm yours."
ngpp: Even buttoned in nothing but your oversized shirt, she pauses mid-stride across the rug, shivering with a sudden flash of heat she can't explain.
"Okay, laugh at me," she breathes right against your chin, hips rocking gently in your lap. "Why does straddling you in this shirt already feel like my favorite habit?"
"Reset the cycle all she wants," Hanna whispers fiercely, unbuttoning the stolen shirt right in your palms. "My body never forgot this bed, Sam. Claim me front page tonight."
hanna.goLead: You peel your shirt up off Hanna's freckled shoulders and lay her back on the sheets. She's laughing, and then the laugh turns into a low, eager gasp against your throat.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Hanna blinks, swallows hard, and manages a crooked smile as she climbs off your lap. "Okay," she says softly, pulling the oversized shirt tighter around herself. "Wait's on the record. Just don't keep a girl on hold too long."
